system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Seller Position Review

## Departures from Wattlebridge's Playbook

The Seller's package departs from our internal positions in several material ways. Below are the key issues, ordered by severity.

### A. General warranty cap (Clause 12.1) – 20% / AUD 4,800,000
The Seller proposes a fixed 20% cap **without acknowledging the Amelia Frost pre-approval requirement**. Under our playbook, 25% / AUD 6,000,000 is the starting position and 20% / AUD 4,800,000 is conditional fallback requiring prior written authority from our principal — which has not been granted. This departure is potentially fatal to our default position.

### B. Time limits (Clause 12.3) – 18 months general claims
Same path as (A): the Seller defaults to 18 months without reference to the Amelia Frost approval pathway the playbook mandates. Twenty-four months is our standing default; 18 months is a fallback none of our principals have signalled.

### C. Thresholds (Clause 12.2) – de minimis AUD 25,000, basket AUD 250,000
Both thresholds are set higher than our preferred parameters, which favours the seller at the de minimis gate (more claims actionable sooner) and at the basket gate (less recoverable amount once reached). These are departures in the wrong direction for buyer protection, and there is no mechanism for us to request a reset.

### D. Title / fundamental claims consolidated (Clause 12.3 / 13)
The Seller collapses fundamental and title warranties into the general regime. Our playbook requires a **separate 100%-cap regime, at least six years, outside the basket/de minimis/knowledge bar**. Consolidation materially dilutes the buyer's strongest warranty category.

### E. Disclosure (Schedule 7) – general deemed disclosure
The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers. The playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure. This is a formal breach of our disclosure standard.

### F. Clause 8.3 – blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
The Seller's language ("Buyer shall have no claim … including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records") reproduces the very blanket exclusion we want deleted. Any qualifier — if we accept one — must name a specific knowledge person and demonstrate a reasonable enquiry; the Seller offers nothing of the kind.

### G. Bluefen (Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) makes this a material customer. The Seller states the consent is satisfied only on delivery of written consent, with no evidence associated conditions have been satisfied and no effective consent included. Reasonable endeavour is insufficient for a material customer consent under our playbook — we need effective consent **before** Completion, with satisfied conditions evidenced. This is a significant gap.

### H. Riverlark (Clause 2 / 7)
The release is described as "following Completion." The playbook requires **current repayment from Completion funds plus effective security releases**, and any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval. The Seller does not address either the current payout or the irrevocable undertaking.

### I. Funds flow – DD-005 bonuses excluded
The Seller declines to itemise the AUD 420,000 closing bonuses in the completion funds flow and states the disclosure does not confirm whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply. Under DD-005, those items **must be a specific line item or seller-funded** and the triggered on-costs must be reflected. Silent exclusion is a material omission.

### J. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1)
The Seller defends the narrow indemnity as adequate and preserves the SOW3 payment-on-cleared-payment condition. The playbook explicitly says to **broaden** the indemnity while preserving the cure. The AUD 180,000 open (not independently bank-verified) is acknowledged by the Seller — a responsible posture — but the Seller refuses the broader remedy.

### K. Title (Clause 4)
DD-012 is identified as the sole title evidence. Under our playbook the register is an **supplied internal source, not independent proof**; we require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. This is a soft exit on a material asset.

### L. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
The Seller classifies them automatically as ordinary-course operating costs without substantiation. The playbook instructs us to **assess** them — an assessment could expose a debt/price-deduction risk the Seller is foreclosing on by shortcutting the determination.

### M. Tax / IP – settled under general regime
The Seller settles both Tax and IP warranties under the general 20%-cap framework, treating them as "settled." The playbook leaves these terms **open** and warns to assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. Conflating IP/tax into the general regime creates latent unlimited-liability exposure we have not agreed to.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

1. **Rise to the 20%/AUD 4.8M cap.** Demand the Seller maintain 25%/AUD 6,000,000 as the default, retain 20% as the conditional Amelia-Frost-gated fallback, and delete the cap increase unilaterally without our written authority.

2. **Restore the 24-month general claims period** as the default; delete the 18-month fallback unless our principal authorises it in writing, specifying the draft identification.

3. **Correct thresholds** — lower de minimis and basket toward the playbook's safer parameters, or at minimum give us a right to renegotiate.

4. **Split title/fundamental from general.** Restore the separate 100%-cap, six-year regime outside the basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

5. **Carve fraud and wilful concealment out of the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses** — including all baskets, caps and time limits — and ensure the Seller cannot waive
=== END ADVICE ===
